request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheets of a tree now share one claim number sequence, and all 4 tests in the acceptance spec pass under `bin/e2e`.

**How it works now:** when a claim is opened on a sheet that isn't using per-period numbering, it gets one more than the highest number given on any sheet in its tree. The tree is the topmost parent and everything below it, found with the existing `SettingRepository.tree()`. Numbers already given stay as they are. Per-period numbers like `P1-1` still count separately on each sheet.

**What changed:** two files, and no database changes.
- `ClaimRepository.nextNumber(sheetId, tree)` reads the last-number counter of every sheet in the tree, takes the highest, and stores that plus one as this sheet's counter.
- To stop two claims opened at the same moment in the same tree from getting the same number, it locks those counters until the transaction ends. It always locks them in the same order (sorted by sheet id) so two openings can't block each other.
- `ClaimNumbering.next` passes the sheet's tree in. Every place that hands out a number goes through it, so opening, splitting, reassigning, cloning and transferring a person all use the shared sequence.

One thing to be aware of: a sheet's counter is only checked against the rest of the tree when a claim is opened on it. So if a sheet joins a tree after its own numbers have run ahead, the next claim opened anywhere in the tree continues after the highest number, which is what the request asks for.
